skill.name: superpower-zustand
skill.description: Build type-safe Zustand stores with a StoreBuilder pattern that separates state, actions, persistence, and non-reactive access.
skill.summary: Creates standardized Zustand stores with Immer updates, optional persistence, and separated factory actions.

content.value_statement: Zustand stores often become inconsistent when actions, persistence, and updates follow different patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward one StoreBuilder approach.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of Zustand stores using a StoreBuilder utility.
Separates state fields from action methods with factory-based store creation.
Shows Immer-style draft mutations for safer state updates.
Documents optional persistence settings, including storage keys and partial state selection.
Provides examples for React hooks and non-reactive get, set, and subscribe access.
limitations: Applies only to React projects that use Zustand.
Requires compatible Zustand and Immer middleware packages in the project.
Does not validate generated code against a live TypeScript compiler.
Persistence guidance still requires careful selection of safe fields.

use_cases.title: Create Feature Stores
use_cases.description: Build a new typed store with separate state, actions, and optional persistence.

use_cases.title: Refactor Existing Stores
use_cases.description: Convert inline Zustand actions into a consistent StoreBuilder factory structure.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Patterns
use_cases.description: Document one repeatable store architecture for teams using Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Store
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Zustand store for a counter using the StoreBuilder pattern. Include state, actions, and the exported hook.

prompt_templates.title: Add Persisted Preferences
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a preferences store with theme and language fields. Use StoreBuilder persistence and persist only safe preference values.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor an Existing Store
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my existing Zustand store to use StoreBuilder. Separate state from actions and keep the public hook API stable.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Async Domain Store
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a StoreBuilder-based store for asynchronous todo loading. Include loading, error, mutation actions, and non-reactive access guidance.

output_examples.input: Create a cart store with add, remove, and clear actions.
output_examples.output: A typed Zustand store structure with cart state, factory actions, Immer updates, and an exported hook.

output_examples.input: Add persistence for user preferences only.
output_examples.output: A persistence plan that stores safe preference fields while avoiding sensitive or temporary state.

output_examples.input: Review whether my store follows the required pattern.
output: State fields are separated from actions.
Actions are created through the factory.
Persistence is limited to appropriate fields.

best_practices: Copy the StoreBuilder utility into a shared project location before creating stores.
Keep persisted fields narrow and avoid storing sensitive data.
Review generated stores with TypeScript checks and application tests.
anti_patterns: Mixing action methods into the initial state object.
Persisting entire stores when only preferences or identifiers need storage.
Using non-reactive state access inside React components when a hook selector is clearer.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create Zustand stores that use a shared StoreBuilder utility, Immer updates, and separated action factories.

faq.question: Does it install Zustand or Immer?
faq.answer: No. The project must already include compatible Zustand and Immer middleware packages.

faq.question: Can it support persisted state?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents optional persistence with storage names, versions, custom storage, and partial state selection.

faq.question: Can it refactor an existing store?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide a refactor from inline Zustand actions to a StoreBuilder factory pattern.

faq.question: Does it work outside React components?
faq.answer: Yes. The pattern exposes non-reactive get, set, and subscribe access for utility code or side effects.

faq.question: Should persisted fields include secrets?
faq.answer: No. Persist only low-risk preferences or identifiers, and avoid sensitive user data.
